subject: 🏃 Thursday — 7 mi Progression Run, Esplanade (Wk 5)
html:
Tomorrow: 7 mi Progression Run on the Esplanade — 5 mi easy @ 9:00, then 2 mi threshold by HR (155–162, cap 165; target pace 7:15–7:25). This is the same Esplanade you ran Tuesday's threshold on, and it's flat — clean signal, no terrain confounders. Pre-run PT block + activation in the hotel room: hip CARs, banded lateral walks, glute bridges, plus quadruped banded hip IR (5–10 reps each side). Jet lag should be mostly absorbed by day 4 — your body clock is nearly synced.

The knee headline: you logged 2/5 today — mild awareness on stairs after Heavy Strength, resolved quickly. That's the first non-1 reading in the entire V6 build. At a 2, the protocol says train as planned but double the mobility flush. Tomorrow's run is ON, but with a gate: do the pre-run activation, start the easy miles, and check in with the knee at mile 1. If it's 1/5 and quiet, continue as written — 5 easy, then flip to threshold for the final 2. If it's still talking at mile 1, stay easy for all 7 and skip the threshold close. If it's 3+ at any point, stop and bike instead. Don't push through awareness to chase the threshold stimulus — Tuesday already banked 5 threshold miles, so the weekly dose is covered.

Execution: run the BU Bridge ↔ Mass Ave Bridge stretch for the threshold miles — you know the footing now and it's dead flat. HR is the anchor: hold 155–162 for the threshold portion, accept whatever pace that gives you. Yesterday's squat session + cumulative travel-week fatigue may depress pace at correct HR — that's Wed→Thu post-lift drag, and it's expected. Log the pace but don't chase it.

Focus cue: knee awareness check at every mile marker. Not anxiously — just a quick internal read. Today's 2/5 came from stairs after a heavy session, not from running, and it cleared fast. But the first run after a non-1 knee reading deserves deliberate attention.

Context: Week 5 of 12, Phase 2 (Strength & Threshold) — 52 days to the SF Marathon. Tuesday's Esplanade session was the cleanest threshold work of this Boston week (5 reps, HR capped at 163, knee 1/5). Today's strength pushed the squat to 175 Good and unlocked calf raises on the barbell at 155. The knee's 2/5 is the price tag for a big strength day — expected, not alarming, but it sets the monitoring posture for tomorrow.

Tonight: Double the mobility flush — foam roll quads and IT band 2 min each, 90/90 switches, couch stretch 90 sec each side. Hydrate well (hotel air + post-lift). Bed by 10 PM ET. Tomorrow is your last Boston run before Friday's flight home — make it a clean one.
